_meta.description: Analytical 1–5 scores (assessment, not measurement). 5 = clear leadership with durable evidence; 3 = competitive parity; 1 = structural disadvantage. 'Microsoft' scores its own models and distribution; OpenAI is scored separately. 'Open-weight' is the ecosystem (Qwen, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Mistral).

rubric.5: Clear leadership; evidence in filings or independent data
rubric.4: Strong; near the top with some contest

dimensions.anthropicEvidence: Opus 5.5 SWE-bench Pro 89.9% (vendor); #1 AA v4 snapshot (58); Mythos gated for capability.
dimensions.counterargument: GPT-6 Astra leads some agentic benchmarks; Gemini 4 Carbon claims; Kimi K3.1 Pro within points on AA v4.
dimensions.whatErodes: A rival leapfrog for two consecutive release cycles.

dimensions.anthropicEvidence: Claude Code 'default' in enterprise eng orgs; top-5% users ≈20× spend; Claude Code + Codex ≈70% of coding spend.
dimensions.counterargument: Copilot Fusion claims parity within 2 pts at −50% cost; Codex ~40M combined users; Cursor/Composer on open weights.
dimensions.whatErodes: Routing layers that make the model invisible to developers.

dimensions.anthropicEvidence: >90% of code by Claude; 250 launches in 9M; ExploitBench 40%→91% in ~4 months.
dimensions.counterargument: RSP thresholds may add human review; OpenAI and Google DeepMind research depth.

dimensions.anthropicEvidence: Implied ~85% gross margin on serving; ex short-term compute ~29% of revenue.
dimensions.counterargument: Google's vertically integrated TPU serving; open-weight serving at ~$0.13/M tokens.
dimensions.whatErodes: Price cuts that pass gains to customers.

dimensions.anthropicEvidence: Revenue +1,127% vs compute +382% YoY; compute multipliers.
dimensions.counterargument: ≥74% of compute goes to research/development; no disclosure of training cost per model.
dimensions.whatErodes: Rivals' algorithmic advances diffusing via papers and distillation.

dimensions.anthropicEvidence: Four chip families natively; $895.4B committed; multi-supplier leverage.
dimensions.counterargument: TPU-heavy commitments; Q3 surge premium; $213.8B contingent on suppliers.
dimensions.whatErodes: Supplier financing failures or demand shortfall.

dimensions.anthropicEvidence: >50% of F500 at ≥$100K; all three clouds; SIs; 150,000 certified practitioners.
dimensions.counterargument: Incumbents own workflows (M365, Workspace); <0.1% of F500 expenses.

dimensions.anthropicEvidence: MCP standard; Agent SDK; Claude Code adoption; developer-led entry pattern.
dimensions.counterargument: MCP donated to Linux Foundation (open); developers switch models fast (>80% revenue from <6-month-old models).
dimensions.whatErodes: Harness commoditization; GitHub control of the dev loop.

dimensions.anthropicEvidence: Enterprise Frontier Safeguards; gated releases; PBC/LTBT governance.
dimensions.counterargument: 5–7% violating revenue; U.S. supply-chain-risk designation; export restrictions disabled flagship models.
dimensions.whatErodes: A major safety incident or prolonged government dispute.

dimensions.anthropicEvidence: $146.6B liquidity; +$6.6B operating cash flow; $77B partner financing; IPO.
dimensions.counterargument: ≈$105B/yr of obligations through 2030; covenants; dependence on partner capital.
dimensions.whatErodes: Revenue slowdown before capacity is absorbed.
